extracted.intended_audience: employers, human resources professionals, labor law attorneys, and compliance officers responsible for FLSA exemptions
extracted.subtask_description: Federal regulatory criteria (29 CFR part 541) defining salary/compensation tests, thresholds, exceptions, and update procedures for executive, administrative, professional, computer, and outside sales exemptions under the Fair Labor Standards Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Severability (§541.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: The provisions of this part are separate and severable and operate independently from one another. If any provision is held invalid or unenforceable by its terms, or as applied to any person or circumstance, or stayed pending further agency action, the provision must be construed so as to continue to give the maximum effect permitted by law, unless the holding is one of utter invalidity or unenforceability, in which event the provision will be severable from part 541 and will not affect the remainder thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Doctrine to preserve as much of the regulation as possible if parts are invalidated; no substantive examples beyond legal construction guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive employee salary requirement (§541.100(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: An executive employee must be compensated on a salary basis at not less than the level set forth in §541.600.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Amends prior text to reference §541.600 rather than a specific dollar figure; applies as a gating salary test in addition to duties tests (see cross‑refs to §§541.100, 541.200, 541.300).

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative employee salary/fee requirement (§541.200(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: An administrative employee must be compensated on a salary or fee basis at not less than the level set forth in §541.600.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows payment on a fee basis for administrative employees where §541.605 applies; links the administrative exemption to the standard salary level in §541.600.

rubrics_metrics.name: Educational establishments salary alternative (§541.204(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Employees of educational establishments may be compensated on a salary or fee basis at not less than the level set forth in §541.600; or on a salary basis which is at least equal to the entrance salary for teachers in the educational establishment by which employed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides a tailored alternative salary test for academic settings: either meet §541.600 level or equal the institution's teacher entrance salary (see §541.600(e)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Professional employee salary/fee requirement (§541.300(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: A professional employee must be compensated on a salary or fee basis at not less than the level set forth in §541.600.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Links professional exemption to standard salary level; note that certain professional categories have exceptions (see §541.600(g)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Computer employee salary/fee requirement (§541.400(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: The section 13(a)(1) exemption applies to any computer employee who is compensated on a salary or fee basis at not less than the level set forth in §541.600.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also provides alternate hourly test for computer employees (§541.600(f)); updates cross‑references to §541.600.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard salary level general rule (§541.600(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: To qualify as an exempt executive, administrative, or professional employee under section 13(a)(1) of the Act, an employee must be compensated on a salary basis at a rate per week of not less than the amounts set forth in paragraphs (a)(1) through (3) of this section, exclusive of board, lodging or other facilities, unless paragraph (b) or (c) applies.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Administrative and professional employees may alternatively be paid on a fee basis as defined in §541.605; the standard salary level is the gating monetary test in addition to duties tests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standard salary level amounts (2024–2027) (§541.600(a)(1)-(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) Beginning July 1, 2024, $844 per week (20th percentile of weekly earnings of full‑time nonhourly workers in the lowest‑wage Census Region and/or retail industry nationally). (2) Beginning January 1, 2025, $1,128 per week (35th percentile of weekly earnings of full‑time nonhourly workers in the lowest‑wage Census Region). (3) As of July 1, 2027, the level calculated pursuant to §541.607(b)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies phased dollar thresholds and references future periodic update methodology for dates after 2027.

rubrics_metrics.name: Special salary levels for U.S. territories (§541.600(b)-(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands, Guam, Puerto Rico, U.S. Virgin Islands: not less than $455 per week for non‑federal employers. American Samoa: not less than $380 per week for non‑federal employers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These special rates apply to non‑Federal employers in the listed territories; the Department declined in this final rule to apply the standard salary level to certain territories and will address in a future final rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frequency of payment translation (§541.600(d))
rubrics_metrics.description: The salary level requirement may be translated into equivalent amounts for periods longer than one week (e.g., biweekly, semimonthly, monthly). However, the shortest period of payment that will meet this compensation requirement is one week.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gives concrete conversion examples (e.g., $1,128/week → $2,256 biweekly, $2,444 semimonthly, $4,888 monthly); emphasizes weekly as the minimal acceptable payment period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative salary level for academic administrative employees (§541.600(e))
rubrics_metrics.description: For academic administrative employees, the salary level requirement may also be met by compensation on a salary basis at a rate at least equal to the entrance salary for teachers in the educational establishment by which the employee is employed (as provided in §541.204(a)(1)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides an academic alternative tied to institution teacher starting pay rather than the standard numeric threshold.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hourly rate alternative for computer employees (§541.600(f))
rubrics_metrics.description: In the case of computer employees, the compensation requirement also may be met by compensation on an hourly basis at a rate not less than $27.63 an hour.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Offers an hourly alternative specific to computer occupations in lieu of the weekly salary/fee test.

rubrics_metrics.name: Exceptions to the standard salary criteria (§541.600(g))
rubrics_metrics.description: Compensation requirements do not apply to certain professionals: teachers (see §541.303); employees who hold a valid license or certificate permitting the practice of law or medicine and are actually engaged in practice (see §541.304); employees with the requisite academic degree for general practice of medicine engaged in internships or residencies (see §541.304). In medical occupations, the exception from the salary or fee requirement does not apply to pharmacists, nurses, therapists, technologists, sanitarians, dietitians, social workers, psychologists, psychometrists, or other professions which service the medical profession.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identifies categories exempt from salary/fee minima; cross‑references duties and other subparts for detail on teachers and professionals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Highly compensated employee (HCE) total compensation test (§541.601(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: An employee shall be exempt under section 13(a)(1) if the employee receives total annual compensation not less than the amounts set forth in paragraph (a)(1) through (4) of §541.601 and customarily and regularly performs one or more of the exempt duties or responsibilities of an executive, administrative, or professional employee identified in subpart B, C, or D.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: HCE test uses total annual compensation as an alternative pathway to exemption but still requires performance of exempt duties; see annual thresholds and composition rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: HCE dollar thresholds (§541.601(a)(1)-(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: (1) Beginning July 1, 2024, $132,964 per year (annualized 80th percentile of full‑time nonhourly workers nationally). (2) Beginning January 1, 2025, $151,164 per year (annualized 85th percentile of full‑time nonhourly workers nationally). (3) As of July 1, 2027, total annual compensation level calculated pursuant to §541.607(b)(2).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies HCE monetary thresholds and references periodic update methodology for 2027 onward.

rubrics_metrics.name: HCE composition and reconciliation rule (§541.601(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Total annual compensation must include at least a weekly amount equal to that required by §541.600(a)(1) through (3) paid on a salary or fee basis as set forth in §§541.602 and 541.605 (with one noted exception for §541.602(a)(3) not applying to HCEs). If total annual compensation falls short by the last pay period of the 52‑week period, the employer may make one final payment during the last pay period or within one month after the end of the 52‑week period to achieve the required level; such payment counts only toward the prior year's total.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes example of employer reconciling anticipated commissions with actual earnings and timing rules for final payments and year attribution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Partial satisfaction of salary via nondiscretionary payments (§541.602(a)(3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Up to ten percent of the salary amount required by §541.600(a) through (c) may be satisfied by the payment of nondiscretionary bonuses, incentives, and commissions that are paid annually or more frequently.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Employer may rely on nondiscretionary payments to satisfy up to 10% of the required salary; if short at year end, employer may make one final payment to meet the annualized requirement (§541.602(a)(3)(i)).

rubrics_metrics.name: Minimum guarantee plus extras (§541.604)
rubrics_metrics.description: An exempt employee guaranteed at least the weekly salary (example: $1,128/week) paid on a salary basis may also receive additional compensation such as a one percent commission on sales, a percentage of sales or profits, or compensation for hours worked beyond the normal workweek without losing the exemption. Example: under §541.600(a)(2), an employee guaranteed compensation of at least $1,210 for any week they perform work and who normally works four or five shifts may be paid $350 per shift without violating the $1,128/week salary basis requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explains that guarantee plus variable pay arrangements are compatible with the salary basis test and provides concrete numeric examples tied to the standard salary level.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fee basis testing for administrative/professional employees (§541.605(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: To determine whether a fee payment meets the minimum amount of salary required for exemption, the amount paid will be tested by determining the time worked on the job and whether the fee payment is at a rate that would amount to at least the minimum salary per week if the employee worked 40 hours. Example: an artist paid $600 for a picture that took 20 hours meets the $1,128 minimum since earnings at this rate would yield $1,200 if 40 hours were worked.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides the 40‑hour equivalency test and an illustrative example for fee‑basis compensation calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Regular update mechanism for salary and compensation amounts (§541.607)
rubrics_metrics.description: Initial updates set specified 2024 amounts ($844/week and $132,964/year). As of July 1, 2027, and every 3 years thereafter, standard salary and HCE total annual compensation amounts will be updated to reflect current earnings data by applying the existing methodologies to current CPS MORG data or successor publication. The Secretary must publish notice in the Federal Register at least 150 days before each future update and post the updated amounts on the Wage and Hour Division website by the effective date. A scheduled update may be delayed 120 days if the Secretary separately publishes a notice of proposed rulemaking at least 150 days before the update date; if no final rule is issued by the end of the 120‑day extension, the update takes effect at the end of that period.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifies frequency (every 3 years), data source (most recent 4 quarters of CPS MORG or successor), notice timing (>=150 days), website publication requirement, and a 120‑day delay procedure tied to separate NPRMs proposing changes to thresholds or mechanisms.
